title: Meta's Black Friday price spike will start from a higher floor
dek: Five sources point the same way: Meta was already dearer than last year before Q4, and Black Friday adds a spike of 60 to 85% on top. The brands that came out ahead in 2025 judged the week on cost per purchase, not CPM.
body: Before November even starts, Meta is more expensive than a year ago. Northbeam's weekly CPM has been running about 24% above last year, and Meta's own earnings show the average price per ad up 14% in Q3. Common Thread's brands paid $17.13 in October 2025 and $21.55 in November, a 26% jump in a single month.

Black Friday stacks a spike on that base. Lebesgue tracked the median Meta CPM at 84% above its September level on Black Friday 2025, with fashion and footwear up 66% and home up 116%. Triple Whale's BFCM average was $22.26, up about 7.8% on 2024.

But the expensive week was not the bad week. In the same Lebesgue data, cost per purchase fell 20% over Black Friday week because conversion rates rose 48%. Northbeam's caution is the exception: Black Friday was the one BFCM day where efficiency fell in 2025.

What to do with it: set Black Friday-week guardrails on CPA or new-customer CAC, not CPM; expect CPMs 60 to 85% above September; and fund prospecting in the first half of November, judged on lagged attribution, so the audience is already warm when prices peak.

title: BFCM 2026: a bigger season, a tighter shopper, an earlier start
dek: Forecasters expect a record season ($275.1B online, Adobe), but most of the growth is price. Shoppers are starting earlier, discounts are anchored at 20 to 40%, and Canadian budgets are shrinking even as Black Friday stays the day that matters.
body: Adobe forecasts US online holiday spend of $275.1B (+6.7%), with Cyber Week at $47.5B and Black Friday the fastest-growing day at $12.9B (+9.2%). Bain expects the BFCM weekend to grow almost twice as fast as the season.

Underneath, unit demand is flat. In 2025 Salesforce saw US Cyber Week orders grow just 1% while prices rose, and this October's consumer sentiment reading was 48.0. Value framing (bundles, gifts with purchase, tiered offers) will do more than deeper discounts: the average Black Friday discount held at 28% last year and 45% of shoppers say 20 to 40% off is enough.

Timing has moved earlier. 71% of shoppers plan to buy before Black Friday and 28% expect their budget to be spent by the end of October. Owned channels carry the peak days (email and SMS were 43% of Klaviyo merchants' revenue), and AI referrals, though small, are growing fastest of any source.
In Canada, budgets are down 6.5% (RCC/Leger) to 14% (Deloitte), but 88% of shoppers rank Black Friday in their top three days and 58% of those affected by trade tensions are avoiding US brands.

title: How many Meta ads should you launch? The answers differ by 10x
dek: Six sources agree that winners are rare (about 1 in 20 ads) and that spend settles on roughly 20 ads per account. They disagree on volume: at $100K a month the recommendations run from about 33 to 300 new ads.
body: The common ground is strong. Motion's 2026 benchmarks (cited by Foxwell, Sicard and Billo) put the hit rate near 5%, rising with spend. MHI's data on 61 DTC brands shows the median brand launching 353 ads a month, yet only about 19 ads take 1% or more of spend, and the top 10 take 39%.

The split is on how many to make. Curtis Howland's rule of one new ad per $3,000 of monthly spend gives about 33 a month at $100K. Billo's Scale tier recommends 80 to 120+, and MHI points towards 100 to 300. At $1M a month the $3,000 rule asks for about 77 a week, four times Motion's measured average of 18.85.
Howland's own caveat is the useful one: volume buys more shots on goal but not a better shot. In one account a 10x jump in AI statics took ROAS down 40%.
